ads.description: Available and Located In Las Vegas Nevada Yes, this is/was a New in The Box 1981 Kural (Exidy Ireland) Samno Crush Roller Cabaret Video Machine. Changed the power plug from 220 to 110. Rebuilt the monitor because it needed it. The video of the April 2026 Unboxing is at www.coinopstuff.com Make Trax, originally released in Japan as Crush Roller (Kurasshu R?r?), is a 1981 maze game developed by Alpha Denshi and published as an arcade video game by Kural Samno Electric in Japan. It was licensed in Europe to Exidy, which released it under its original title Crush Roller, and in North America to Williams Electronics, who released it as Make Trax. The player controls a paintbrush to paint paths within a maze. The player is harassed by two fish, which can be temporarily destroyed by running them over with a one of two paint rollers located near the maze center. A critter occasionally emerges to leave footprints on painted areas, which must then be repainted.

ads.author: Jeanni Perry
ads.title: Buttonbush, Cephalanthus occidentalis
ads.description: https://bellajardins.boutique/product/buttonbush/ My company is Bella Jardins Boutique, an on-line garden shop (no storefront) that specializes in Florida native plants. Orders are made on-line (copy/paste link above to your browser search) then I deliver the plants to you. Sales are limited to only these North Central Florida counties: Baker, Columbia, Union, Alachua, Bradford, Putnam, Clay, St. Johns, and Duval. Total orders that are over $25 before taxes have no delivery fee, orders that are under $25 have a $5 delivery fee. Botanical Name: Cephalanthus occidentalis Common Name: Buttonbush, Honeyballs, Spanish Pincushion, Globeflowers, Swampwood, Button-Willow, Crane Willow, Little Snowball, Pinball, Pond Dogwood Description: Buttonbush is another one of my favorite Florida native shrubs. The fragrant, white ball-shaped flowers look like pincushions and bloom Spring to Summer. In its native habitat, Buttonbush is a wetland shrub, but it adapts to regular garden environments as long as it gets water on a regular basis from either rain or irrigation. Its roots can withstand full submersion in wet areas. I wouldn’t call it a drought tolerant plant. Plant it in that rain garden you’ve been planning, or beside that downspout, or in that low area that stays moist where nothing else will grow, or at the edge of your pond, or in your regular garden beds that get irrigation. It’s fast growing, likes sun, part sun, or part shade, is deciduous, and grows 5 – 12′ tall x 4 – 8′ wide into a loose, rounded habit. The more shade it’s in, the more open the foliage will be. I’ve seen these growing in the wild, and they are glorious plants that are abuzz with butterflies, Titan sphinx moth, Hydrangea sphinx moth, hummers, native bees, honey bees, bumble bees, and all kinds of other pollinators when in bloom, and at least 25 species of birds eat the seeds! You need this shrub in your garden. Is not deer tolerant. Is host plant to several moths including titan sphinx (Aellopos titan) and hydrangea sphinx (Darapsa versicolor) moths. The foliage is poisonous to livestock and people if eaten. It grows in clay, loam, organic material (muck), and sandy soils that are acidic to calcareous. Not salt tolerant of inundation by salty or brackish water. Low/no tolerance of salty wind or direct salt spray. This plant in 3-gallon containers is 2-4′ tall. Plant Lore: The genus Cephalanthus is from the Greek words kephale, or “head,” and ánthos, or “flower.” The species epithet occidentalis is Latin for “west” or “western,” suggesting the plant is native to the western hemisphere. Florida Hardiness Zones 8 – 11

ads.author: John Eric Booth
ads.title: Fully Restored - Operation Thunderbolt Arcade Shooter Game
ads.description: Hey John here from Gameroom Medic! Here is an incredible, fully restored Taito "Operation Thunderbolt" 2-player arcade game from my own collection. It's amazing! This will make someone an outstanding addition to their home arcade and take advantage of a great opportunity! This game is awesome! Last year I performed an intensive, full restoration on this machine... ya gotta see it in person to fully appreciate. This one's from 1989 and let me tell ya, you'd think it's brand new. The coin door was completely disassembled and repainted as well as all coin mechanism parts working perfectly, along with sparkling new vinyl cabinet artwork throughout. Several improvements were made as well including new upper speakers and the addition of a mid-bass speaker and amplifier for added impact! An aluminum footrest (one of my signature mods) replaced the plastic version. New dolly-style casters have been installed. A 25" minty fresh Wells Gardner K7000 monitor provides a stunning picture. The color is vibrant and screen is crystal clear... no burn in! The Uzi machine guns have both been completely disassembled and cleaned. New potentiometers were installed as well. The recoil feature is super fun and works beautifully! Inside the unit is equally impressive. Completely cleaned and painted along with cleaned wiring harnesses. A new power supply has been installed and main PC board fully recapped. This is without a doubt an archive quality machine, completely solid and ready for great game play. I challenge you to find this game in equal condition anywhere! No trades. Cash only. I hate to see this one go but I just don't have room for it. It's big! And heavy! Delivery can be provided but rental of a full liftgate box truck will be necessary. I will not respond to auto-generated messages such as "is this available?" Serious inquiries only please. I welcome your questions, and any respectable offers.

ads.title: Vintage 1979 Taito Space Invaders Part II Cocktail Arcade Cabinet
ads.description: The classic 1980’s video game. This is a vintage 1979 cocktail-style arcade cabinet. It has a wood-grain laminate finish and a glass tabletop. Space Invaders II is the sequel to the original space alien vertical shooter. This is an early Taito direct import from Japan, with Japanese labels. The game was later distributed in North America by Midway as Space Invaders Deluxe. New Gameplay: * Aliens that Split: Certain crab invaders split into two separate shapeshifting units when hit. * Special UFOs: A blinking UFO appears with a random vulnerability state and point values, while later UFOs drop reinforcements. * Save Initials: High score tracking allows players to save their initials for the first time in the series. * Cutscenes: Short animations play between stages showing defeated invaders escaping or sending SOS signals. Power supply, monitor and logic boards have been recapped and tested. Original color CRT. Cabinet is clean and in good condition. No restoration work has been on the cabinet. Coin switch added for freeplay.

Now, fans can experience the legendary battle between Autobots and Decepticons like never before through immersive, action-packed pinball. TRANSFORMERS: More Than Meets the Eye by Stern Pinball is available now in Pro, Premium, and Limited Edition (LE) models. In Stern Pinball’s TRANSFORMERS: More Than Meets the Eye, players join Optimus Prime and the Autobots in their mission to stop Megatron and the Decepticons from stealing Earth’s energy, conquering Cybertron, and dominating the universe. TRANSFORMERS: More Than Meets the Eye pushes mechanical innovation to new heights with a fully animatronic Megatron robot toy with an articulated fusion cannon that rotates and fires pinballs back at players. Players will experience the ultimate battle between Autobots and Deceptions, and can store Energon Cubes to power up, team up with the Dinobots, collect Transformers Tech Spec cards, and prepare for a climactic battle against Megatron. Players embark on missions inspired by major story arcs from the original 1984 TRANSFORMERS animated television series, and the machine integrates authentic video clips and story-driven missions that bring the brand’s legacy to life. To celebrate the 40th anniversary of THE TRANSFORMERS: THE MOVIE, the game includes a special mode featuring the iconic song “The Touch” by Stan Bush, custom call-outs from legendary voice actors including Peter Cullen (Optimus Prime) and Frank Welker (Megatron and Soundwave), and original music from Knights of Unicron. Loaded with Stern Pinball’s cutting-edge technology, TRANSFORMERS: More Than Meets the Eye seamlessly blends physical and digital gameplay. Utilizing Stern’s award-winning Insider Connected platform, the machine introduces a brand-new Cyber Coin wallet system, where players can earn Cyber Coins to unlock exclusive challenge modes. The machine also features a special challenge mode, “Prime Training,” where Autobots guide players through the art of pinball mastery, and for the first time, includes a head-to-head experience that allows two players to compete simultaneously in real time. Limited to 750 games globally, the highly collectible Limited Edition model includes the updated Expression Lighting SystemTM and Speaker Expression Lighting System with TRANSFORMERS-themed game effects, a full-color mirrored backglass, full-color high-definition cabinet decals, exclusive custom pinball armor, a custom designer-autographed bottom arch, upgraded audio system, anti-reflection pinball playfield glass, shaker motor, a sequentially numbered plaque, a signed Certificate of Authenticity, and a digital Insider Connected LE owner’s badge on registration.

ads.author: David Jenkins
ads.title: Super Bug Arcade Fully Working and Restored
ads.description: Price is for SFGE only if I gotta haul it back home the price goes back to $1700 Newly restored Super Bug arcade machine. Made in 1977 by Kee games. Pros Works flawlessly, game board has been serviced and recapped, sound amp has been replaced and audio has been tuned. Power supply has been tested and the big blue capacitor has been replaced. I added a fan with adjustable speed to keep the game pcb cool. Comes with all original artwork and a reproduction bezel, has the original but I’d prefer to keep it in order to make an accurate reproduction for it. Has a newer burn free color Sanyo crt monitor modified to work with the game. Unhacked harness. All modifications to the wiring are plug and play. No cut wires so all work can easily be reversed if you wanted to put the old screen back in. Not sure why you would though. Comes with original manuals for the game and has a printed manual for the new screen. Overall in great shape. One of the nicest looking Super Bugs you can find. Cons Original screen doesn’t work which is why it has been replaced with a working screen Original bezel is cracked and has cigarette burns hence the reproduction bezel made by Sticker Smith. Has some wear and scratch. Missing the original coin box Restoration process was recorded and is available on YouTube at “Jenxed Arcade” Currently for sale and for play at southern fried gaming expo. Feel free send me a message for more info and we can iron out the details!

Both cabinets are built Exactly the same just one is blue and black (Tekken artwork) and one is red and black (Street Fighter artwork). Require almost zero work. Install the JVS compatible system and off you go. They also make converters that make it to where you can install a PC or a game console. ads.author: Rob Schoonmaker
ads.title: Gate Of Doom 1990 Full Size Stand Up Arcade Game
ads.description: Gate of Doom, known in Japan as Dark Seal (ダークシール), is a hack 'n slash game developed by Data East and released in 1990 for arcades. Gate of Doom is a hack 'n slash game which uses a top-down, isometric perspective. Players can choose between four different characters, each with their own characteristics and abilities. The player can move and attack in eight directions, as well as unleash a powerful spell once its accumulated enough magic power. Much like in Karnov, the player can pick between available spells by tapping the joystick left and right. Levels are filled with enemies and traps, as well as treasure chests which the player can open to obtain various items and power-ups which give passive boosts to the character.

ads.author: Joshua Beecham
ads.title: Arcade Cabinet Project - Cabinet Shell and other parts - $200
ads.description: Empty arcade cabinet shell. Perfect restoration project for an arcade enthusiast, retro gamer, or father-and-son build. The cabinet was built from scratch using 3/4" MDF and includes: 32" portrait-mounted TV with Lexan bezel Marquee fluorescent light Cabinet shell The TV has older inputs including VGA and DVI, and may also have HDMI. Please note: the cabinet has been stored on a screened porch for several years and is dusty. It will need cleaning and some refurbishment before being put back into service. I originally built this for myself and planned to build another one someday, so I removed many of the reusable components when I retired it. It worked perfectly when I disassembled it all. We can some testing from my back porch if you want. Cabinet shell + TV + marquee light: $50 or make offer Optional components available separately: Mini-fridge - $35 Fits perfectly in the bottom of the cabinet. Holds roughly 18-24 cans. Speakers and Amplifier - $25 Generic car speakers and cheap amp. Nothing fancy, but they sounded great in the cabinet. Control Panel - $100 This was the most labor-intensive part of the build. Includes: 12 quality arcade buttons Dual joysticks Trackball Mini-PAC Opti USB controller The Mini-PAC Opti alone sells for around $69 new. The trackball has a cracked plastic piece that will need repair or replacement. Arcade PC - $30 Windows XP machine configured to boot directly into a MAME front end. The hardware itself isn't particularly valuable, but the software setup and configuration took significant time. You could also replace it with a Raspberry Pi running RetroPie or another arcade emulator solution. Pricing Summary Cabinet + TV + marquee light: $50/make offer Mini-fridge: $35 Speakers + amp: $25 Control panel: $100 Arcade PC: $30 Take everything for $200. or make offer The cabinet itself priced low because I need the space. The accessories are the parts I'd originally planned to keep for a future build, but my wife would be thrilled if they disappeared too. Pickup is only available between 6pm and 9pm weekdays and most anytime next weekend. No delivery. You will need your own truck or SUV. I expect this to be gone after Sunday July 26th. This is less of an arcade machine and more of a starting point if you want to *make* one. I offer no guarantees or support.
